messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Incident opened: High tail latency observed for streaming inference endpoints (p99 > 3s). Alert rule: runtime.streaming.latency.p99 > 2.5s for 5m. Impact: multiple customers reporting stalls / partial responses. Paging oncall: @Marcus Li
Marcus Li: On it. ACKing page. Pulling up dashboards now.
Marcus Li: Quick summary from Grafana: p95 ~ 400ms, p99 jumped to ~3.6s across eu-west-1 & us-central-1 starting ~1835011200. Streaming stall count spiking.
Jenna Roberts: Adding context — support ticket 8372 reports partial stream (client got headers then stuck). Might be tokenization/decode backpressure or KV cache miss storms. @Marcus can you paste the host-level metrics?
Marcus Li: Fetching runtime /metrics for model-serving pool: ```curl -s http://infra-metrics.internal/rows?pool=serving-eu-west | jq '.[] | {host, p99, kv_evict, kv_prefill, decode_cpu}'```
Marcus Li: Result (trimmed): ```[{"host":"srv-euw-03","p99":3.8,"kv_evict":1298,"kv_prefill":45,"decode_cpu":82},{"host":"srv-euw-07","p99":4.1,"kv_evict":1420,"kv_prefill":12,"decode_cpu":90}]```
Alice Chen: Those kv_prefill numbers are suspiciously low vs evict. Prefill should be ~prefill_rate 200/s for warm cache, not single digits. Looks like prefill tasks are starving or being cancelled. Fragmentation metric: `kv_fragmentation_ratio` showing 0.71 on affected hosts.
Tomás García: Also seeing continuous small eviction bursts in logs: `kv_cache:evict key_count=120 size_bytes=14MB reason=fragmentation`. That suggests lots of small segments being evicted, not long-lived prefixes.
Jenna Roberts: Could be prefill vs decode imbalance — decode threads are saturated, so prefill tasks get deprioritized, leading to many misses and then immediate evictions when prefill finally fires. Decode CPU ~85-95% on those hosts confirms it.
Marcus Li: Rolling tail logs from srv-euw-07: ```[1835011254] decode:start req=abcd user=acct-12 tokens_in=800 tokens_out=40
[1835011255] kv:cache_miss key=prefix_123
[1835011256] prefill:start key=prefix_123
[1835011260] decode:cpu_wait
[1835011265] prefill:complete size=3MB
[1835011266] kv:evict key=prefix_999 reason=overcommit
[1835011267] stream:stall req=abcd duration=12s
```
support-bot: Support ticket 8372 updated: "Customers A, B seeing streaming stalls; degraded throughput for /v1/stream endpoints."
Marcus Li: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) throttle large decode requests to reduce CPU pressure 2) temporarily raise kv_cache_capacity on affected pools 3) change eviction policy to favor larger prefixes (if available) 4) disable aggressive prefill cancellation. Thoughts?
Alice Chen: I prefer increasing cache capacity + reducing prefill cancellation first. Throttling decode needs careful rate-limiting so we don't break SLAs for normal traffic. We can also route high-token requests to lower-tier pool with looser latency SLO but more capacity.
Tomás García: Quick check: can we bump kv_cache capacity on srv-euw-03/07 by +20% via SRE autoscale? If it's a local config we can push a hotfix. Also, metric `kv_mem_used` is at 96% just before the evictions.
Marcus Li: I'm going to run a hot-config change to +25% on pool serving-eu-west for cache_size. Will run canary on srv-euw-03 only first. Command: ```infractl pool update serving-eu-west --cache-size +25% --host srv-euw-03```
Jenna Roberts: I'll prepare fallback route for large requests: add a routing rule to send requests with input_tokens > 1000 to serving-eu-west-burst which has dedicated capacity. Patch: ```routes: - match: input_tokens > 1000 action: route: serving-eu-west-burst```
infra-bot: Submitted job infractl-20394: pool update job queued. Canaries: srv-euw-03. ETA 30s.
Marcus Li: Can confirm canary applied. Monitoring for immediate regression.
Marcus Li: Post-canary metrics (5m window): srv-euw-03 p99 down from 3.8s -> 1.2s, kv_evict down 1298 -> 210, kv_prefill bumped 45 -> 220. Good signal.
Alice Chen: Nice. That suggests capacity helped reduce churn. But fragmentation still 0.65 on srv-euw-07. Need host-level fix.
Tomás García: For longer-term, we should adjust prefill scheduler priority to prevent cancellation during decode spikes. Currently prefill tasks are CPU-low-priority; maybe change to I/O-bound priority so they get scheduled even if decoders are busy.
Jenna Roberts: Also, metric correlation shows spikes aligned with customer B's batch infer jobs at 1835011000-1835011400 — large batched inputs (many short queries) create many small prefixes, causing fragmentation. We should talk to CS about limiting batch concurrency or moving those jobs to dedicated capacity. @support-bot can you reach out?
support-bot: Noted. Creating outreach play: recommend dedicated capacity or scheduled off-peak windows to reduce tail impact. Ticket updated.
Marcus Li: Next steps I'm taking now: 1) promote cache-size +25% to whole pool (serving-eu-west) 2) enable routing rule to divert >1000 token requests 3) adjust prefill cancellation flag to reduce cancellations for 60s window. Doing 1 now.
Marcus Li: Pool update in progress. infra-bot: job infractl-20395 queued for full pool rollout. ETA 2m.
Marcus Li: Rolling update completed. Preliminary pool metrics: p99 cluster-wide down from 3.6s -> 900ms, streaming stall count down 82% in last 10m.
Alice Chen: Good. For postmortem: collect traces for evicted keys to see lifetime distribution, capture prefill queue depth, and quantify prefill vs decode CPU scheduling. Also evaluate if LFU eviction would help vs LRU given many small hot prefixes.
Tomás García: I'll open an RFC for: 1) prefill scheduler redesign (IO-priority, backpressure signals), 2) adaptive cache sizing based on fragmentation ratio, 3) route-based isolation for high-token jobs.
Jenna Roberts: For customer comms: I've drafted a note explaining transient latency due to cache churn and our mitigations (bumped cache size, routing adjustments). @support-bot will send to affected accounts after ops confirms stability.
support-bot: Draft ready, awaiting final ack.
Marcus Li: Handing off oncall to Jenna — system stable but continuing to monitor 30m. Jenna, please take over.
Jenna Roberts: Ack — taking oncall. I'll watch p99, kv_evict, kv_prefill, and fragmentation. If p99 > 2s again, escalate to SRE and start rollback of recent deploys.
incident-bot: Incident status changed to: mitigated (partial). Monitoring for 1h before close.
Marcus Li: Quick note for post-incident: capture timeline, config changes (cache +25%, routing rule for >1000 tokens, prefill cancellation disabled 60s), and affected customer list. I'll add logs and command outputs to the incident doc.
Alice Chen: Also include recommended next steps: run controlled experiment for LFU vs LRU on staging, and add alert for kv_fragmentation_ratio > 0.6.
Jenna Roberts: Copy. I'll keep this thread updated and close when monitoring window passes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
